record.part_note: Everything below was read off datasheet.pdf IN THIS FOLDER — ST DS12484 Rev 8 (May 2023, 160 pages), fetched 2026-09-02, sha256 1170f4d74ff501917262ae42bf81c60c38c11d121e2ea2af6b1e845433befef1 (PROVENANCE.json) — via `pdftotext -layout`; quotes are that extraction with whitespace collapsed and tools/datasheet-quotes-check.py re-finds each in the PDF. The document covers ST25R3916 AND ST25R3917; this record is the ST25R3916 (the member with EMVCo and card-emulation; p.1 Table 1 lists the differences).
record.description: 13.56 MHz NFC universal device: reader/writer for NFC-A/B/F/V, card emulation (NFC-A/F), active and passive P2P, EMVCo 3.0 reader; integrated regulators, 512-byte FIFO, SPI up to 10 Mbit/s or I2C up to 3.4 Mbit/s host interface; can drive two independent single-ended antennas. p.1 title verbatim: 'High performance NFC universal device and EMVCo reader'.
record.description_quote: High performance NFC universal device and EMVCo reader

record.package: VFQFPN32 (5x5 mm, wettable flanks, suffix QW), UFQFPN32 (5x5 mm, suffix QE), WLCSP36 (suffix WL) — p.1 package figure 'VFQFPN32 UFQFPN32 WLCSP36' with '(5x5 mm) (5x5 mm)'; §7 Ordering information verbatim 'QW = 32-pin VFQFPN (5 x 5 mm) with wettable flanks'.

record.rails_why: VDD/VDD_TX accept 2.4–5.5 V and VDD_IO 1.65–5.5 V (Table 119), so both the Radxa's 3.3 V and a 5 V rail are inside the window; 3V3 named here because the Radxa Zero 3W header I2C/SPI is 3.3 V logic.
record.absolute_max: p.136 Table 118 'Absolute maximum ratings', rows verbatim: 'Positive supply voltage -0.3 6.0' (VDD, VDD_TX, V); 'Positive supply voltage when option bit sup3V is set -0.3 5'; 'Peripheral communication supply voltage -0.3 6' (VDD_IO); 'Total power dissipation (all supplies and outputs) - 300 mW'; 'Junction temperature -40 125' (°C); 'Storage temperature -65 150'.
absolute_max_quotes: Total power dissipation (all supplies and outputs) - 300 mW

supplies.name: VDD / VDD_TX
supplies.cite: p.137 Table 119 'Operating conditions', rows verbatim: 'Positive supply voltage (pins 8 and 10), 2.6 5.5 Tamb = -40 to 105 °C, rege <3:0> ≥ 07h' and 'Positive supply voltage (pins 8 and 10), 2.4 5.5 Tamb = -20 to 105 °C'. 2.4 V is the -20 °C floor, 2.6 V the -40 °C floor. No TYP column exists in Table 119 — v_typ null by observation. With option bit sup3V set the ceiling drops to 3.6 V (same table).
supplies.quote: Positive supply voltage (pins 8 and 10), 2.6 5.5 Tamb = -40 to 105 °C, rege <3:0> ≥ 07h

supplies.name: VDD_IO
supplies.cite: p.137 Table 119 row verbatim: 'Peripheral communication supply voltage (pin 1)(4) 1.65 5.5' — the host-interface (SPI/I2C) supply, which is what sets the logic levels toward the Radxa.

current_mA.rail_basis: VDD/VDD_TX and VDD_IO all on 3.3 V is the Radxa-header case.
current_mA.typical_basis: NOT TRANSCRIBED. The sheet's current figures live in Table 121 'ST25R3916/7 electrical characteristics (VDD = 3.3 V)' (p.138 ff.) as many operating-mode rows (transmit at a given RFO driver setting, receive, wake-up, power-down) and no single typical exists; a design chooses a mode. The ABSOLUTE ceilings are quoted instead: 'Maximum driver current using internal voltage regulator - 350(4)' mA and 'Peak current supplied from an external source, internal voltage regulator bypassed 500(6)' mA (Table 118).
current_mA.peak_basis: Table 118 row verbatim 'Maximum driver current using internal voltage regulator - 350(4)' (mA; footnote 4 'Provide good thermal management…'). An absolute-maximum RF-driver current, not a measured typical draw.
current_mA.sleep_basis: NOT TRANSCRIBED — power-down / wake-up currents are in Table 121 and were not read into this record.
current_mA.excludes: antenna matching losses; the host MCU
caveats: Field-on current depends entirely on the antenna, matching and driver-resistance setting; the 350 mA figure is a ceiling, not a budget line.
current_mA.cite: p.136 Table 118 rows IVDD_LDO and IVDD_EXT; Table 121 for mode currents (not transcribed).
current_mA.quote: Maximum driver current using internal voltage regulator - 350(4)

logic.cite: Table 120 'Characteristics of CMOS I/Os' was not transcribed; three_v3_tolerant is DERIVED from Table 119 'Peripheral communication supply voltage (pin 1)(4) 1.65 5.5' and Table 118 'Peripheral communication supply voltage -0.3 6' — a 3.3 V VDD_IO is inside both windows.

record.interface_cite: p.1 Features verbatim 'Serial peripheral interface (SPI) up to' … '10 Mbit/s' (the 10 Mbit/s sits on the next extracted line) and 'I2C with up to 400 kbit/s in Fast-mode, 1 Mbit/s in Fast-mode Plus, and 3.4 Mbit/s in High-speed mode'. 10 MHz is the SPI figure; I2C tops out at 3.4 MHz.
